_doc: ABSENCE-SEMANTICS CENSUS — the annotation half of the two-states-one-byte gate.
ONE QUESTION PER ROW: does the ABSENCE of this field mean something DIFFERENT from its
default / empty / null value? If yes the wire needs a discriminator (or the field needs to
be required), because absence and default are otherwise the same byte to a consumer.
distinct   — absence carries a meaning no value can express. NEEDS a discriminator or
required-ness. `ref` must point at the evidence (schema comment, seed
instance, PR/row reference). This is a DEBT ROW, not a resolved one: the
fix rides its own train (most ride 0.28 adoption).
same       — absence is equivalent to the default/empty value. Harmless. `note` must say
why, quoting the contract where it says so.
unresolved — nobody has answered yet. ALLOWED, COUNTED, and pinned by `unresolved_count`
so the debt can shrink but not silently grow.
NEVER GUESS. `distinct` and `same` are seeded ONLY where one of the six seed instances or the
schema's own comment / .describe() makes the answer unambiguous. A plausible-sounding verdict
with no evidence is worse than `unresolved`, because it stops the next reader looking.
THE `fields` KEYS AND `markers` ARE DERIVED, NOT AUTHORED. tests/contracts/absence-semantics/
absence-walk.ts walks the exported Zod graph; the gate diffs this table against that walk and
REDs on any difference in either direction. Editing a key or a marker by hand only breaks the
gate — including changing `optional` to `optional`+`default` on an existing field, which is a
SILENT ABSENCE-SEMANTICS CHANGE and the single most valuable thing this table catches.
The six hand-found instances from the review wave that motivated this gate. Recorded so a
row can cite one, and so the instrument's COVERAGE can be stated precisely rather than
claimed. Four are visible to a schema-side census; two are not, and saying so is the point.

1_cee_may_name_leading_option_provenance.shape: a `true` from "permitted" and a `true` from "blind" are one wire byte
1_cee_may_name_leading_option_provenance.why: ConstraintVerdictSchema.may_name_leading_option is a REQUIRED z.boolean() — no optionality marker, so it is outside this census by construction. The provenance distinction lives in CEE doctrine (MAY_NAME_LEADING_OPTION[state]), which src/orchestrator/handler-results.ts deliberately does not mirror. A required-field-provenance census is a DIFFERENT instrument.

2_cee_fail_closed_uninterpretable.shape: fail-closed marker whose absence and whose false are not the same claim
2_cee_fail_closed_uninterpretable.why: No field of this name exists in @talchain/schemas at 0.28.0 (grepped). It is CEE-internal, so no schema-side instrument in THIS repo can see it. The same SHAPE is visible here and IS caught — see the ABSENCE_FAIL_CLOSED_RULE rows, which are exactly this pattern typed into the contract.

3_plot_meta_constraint_sources.shape: present-but-empty vs absent are different claims, no discriminator
3_plot_meta_constraint_sources.why: Every optional array/record in the contract has this shape. Caught as a row; the resolved example is boundary/DraftGraphBlockSchema.goal_constraints (verdict `same`, because the contract says so out loud), the open example is EnrichmentOptionComparisonEntrySchema.constraint_probabilities.

4_plot_fabricate_on_absence.shape: `?? 0` — absence coalesced into a real-looking measurement
4_plot_fabricate_on_absence.why: Two forms are visible: an optional numeric field a consumer may coalesce (EnrichmentConstraintMarginSchema.failure_margin_median, EnrichmentRobustnessEdgeSchema.switch_probability), and the contract-side twin where the VALIDATOR does the coalescing — a `.default()`, which no consumer can even detect. The census marks the latter with the `default` marker; there is exactly one in the contract today.

5_plot_denormalise_absence_in_absence_ou.shape: a transform that passes absence through, so the output shape is not the input shape
5_plot_denormalise_absence_in_absence_ou.why: The transform itself is PLoT code. Its schema-side signature — a `.transform()` between a declaration and its shape, where the OUTPUT a consumer receives is not derivable from the input schema — is detected by the walker as UNPARSEABLE kind `effects-transform`. There are ZERO such constructs in the contract at 0.28.0, which is itself the finding: the contract never transforms, so every absence it declares reaches the consumer as absence.

6_ui_leading_option_id_null.shape: null treated as the entire withheld contract
6_ui_leading_option_id_null.why: Caught as two rows (the block field and its persisted twin), both `nullable` with the key required, so `null` is the sole channel for every withholding reason. Seeded `distinct`.

_doc: PINNED, and derived from `fields` — the gate recomputes all three and REDs on any mismatch.
`unresolved` is the RATCHET: a new optional field lands as `unresolved`, which forces this
number up IN THE DIFF where a reviewer sees it. It is meant to travel downward.
Objects that accept keys OUTSIDE their declared shape (`.passthrough()` or a catchall), so
the census CANNOT be complete over them by construction — an undeclared key is an
un-enumerable absence. This is workspace-CLAUDE.md hazard 2 (the untyped PLoT->CEE
enrichment seam) measured field by field. The set is PINNED: a new passthrough object is a
new hole in the census and REDs this gate. It shrinks as namespaces are tightened.
By contrast /orchestrator is 100% `.strict()` — every open object below is elsewhere.
Constructs the walker CANNOT introspect: unknown-type, depth-limit,
classification-disagreement, unresolvable-lazy, effects-transform. Each one is a hole in
the census's completeness claim and must be documented here or the gate REDs.
EMPTY AT 0.28.0, and that emptiness is a measured result, not an assumption: 1001 field
sites were visited, and on every one the structural marker classification and Zod's own
isOptional()/isNullable() agreed.

boundary/AnalysisResultBlockSchema.compu.note: Schema comment: "Optional so pinned consumers are unaffected until re-vendored; absent = no computed-against assertion." Absence means NO CLAIM WAS MADE, which is not the same as any hash value — the freshness check must branch on presence, never compare against a fabricated one.

boundary/AnalysisResultBlockSchema.leadi.note: SEED INSTANCE #6 (UI). `z.string().nullable()` — the key is REQUIRED, so `null` is the only channel for every withholding reason at once: a genuine tie, a constraint verdict that forbids naming a leader, and "no analysis ran" are one byte. The discriminator that resolves it already exists on the same wire (ConstraintVerdictSchema.constraint_verdict_state, 0.25.0), but nothing in the contract ties the two together.
boundary/AnalysisResultBlockSchema.leadi.ref: src/boundary/blocks.ts:58 — AnalysisResultBlockSchema.leading_option_id; seed instance #6; discriminator candidate: src/orchestrator/handler-results.ts ConstraintVerdictSchema

boundary/DecisionClassificationSchema.ho.note: Same block comment as stakes: "absence is never defaulted". Horizon is the user's OWN wording, so an empty string and an unassessed horizon are different claims about the user.

boundary/DecisionClassificationSchema.re.note: Same block comment as stakes: "absence is never defaulted". A defaulted `reversible` on an unassessed decision is a fabricated safety claim.

boundary/DecisionClassificationSchema.ri.note: Same block comment as stakes: "absence is never defaulted". Defaulting risk appetite to `balanced` asserts a user stance nobody elicited.

boundary/DecisionClassificationSchema.st.note: Block comment on DecisionClassificationSchema: "a producer states only what it actually assessed, and a consumer renders 'not set' for absent dimensions — partial classification is honest, absence is never defaulted." Per-dimension absence is a first-class state.

boundary/DecisionRecordDecisionSchema.co.note: Schema comment: "Optional; absent means the record predates the commit action (or was auto-captured) — a disclosed inference, never a fabricated value." Absence is explicitly NOT equal to `false`: false asserts ambient capture, absence asserts we cannot tell.

boundary/DecisionRecordPredictionSchema..note: Schema comment: "Both optional-forward: absent whenever no goal target existed at capture." Absence means NO GOAL EXISTED; 0 means the option was measured to miss it. Coalescing the two corrupts every calibration score computed off this record.
boundary/DecisionRecordPredictionSchema..ref: src/boundary/decision-record.ts — DecisionRecordPredictionSchema block comment (0.16.0, D-N Option-B)

boundary/DecisionRecordPredictionSchema..note: Same comment as probability_of_goal: "absent whenever no goal target existed at capture." Absence is a statement about the DECISION, not about the probability.
boundary/DecisionRecordPredictionSchema..ref: src/boundary/decision-record.ts — DecisionRecordPredictionSchema block comment (0.16.0, D-N Option-B)

boundary/DraftGraphBlockSchema.goal_cons.note: Schema comment is explicit and leaves nothing to infer: "Absent when the brief carried none; consumers must treat absence and `[]` as equivalent." This is the SAME SHAPE as seed instance #3 (PLoT `_meta.constraint_sources` present-empty vs absent) — and it is the resolved case: the contract answers the question rather than leaving the consumer to guess.

boundary/EdgeV3Schema.edge_type.note: LEAD — the only `.default()` in the whole contract (src/graph.ts:67, `EdgeType.optional().default('directed')`). A default is `?? 0` promoted into the contract: the VALIDATOR materialises `directed` on absence, so no consumer can ever observe the difference between "the producer modelled this edge as directed" and "the producer said nothing about direction". Whether that difference MATTERS is the unanswered question — record the answer here, do not guess it.

boundary/EnrichmentConstraintMarginSchem.note: Schema block comment: "Absent margin fields are OMITTED, never zeroed — missing != zero (a fabricated 0 read by a live consumer was the exact defect PLoT's producer-honesty gate closed)." This is the contract-side twin of seed instance #4 (PLoT `?? 0` fabricate-on-absence).
boundary/EnrichmentConstraintMarginSchem.ref: src/boundary/enrichment.ts — EnrichmentConstraintMarginSchema block comment; seed instance #4 (PLoT `?? 0`)

boundary/EnrichmentConstraintMarginSchem.note: Field .describe(): "Absent means precision is unknown; consumers MUST NOT assume exactness." Absence names a third state the enum cannot express — the vocabulary is {exact, lower_bound} and "unknown" exists only as key-absence.

Same block comment as failure_margin_median: "Absent margin fields are OMITTED, never zeroed — missing != zero." A rate in [0,1] whose absence is indistinguishable from a measured 0 unless the consumer branches on key presence.
boundary/EnrichmentConstraintMarginSchem.ref: src/boundary/enrichment.ts — EnrichmentConstraintMarginSchema block comment; seed instance #4 (PLoT `?? 0`)

boundary/EnrichmentConstraintResultSchem.note: The field carries the contract-frozen ABSENCE_FAIL_CLOSED_RULE .describe() text: "Absence of this marker means NOT decision-grade (fail-closed). Consumers MUST NOT treat a missing marker as trustworthy." Absence is therefore a TRUST VERDICT, not a missing convenience — and it is carried by the absence of a boolean whose only other state is `true`, so a consumer that defaults it reads untrusted data as trusted.

boundary/EnrichmentOptionComparisonEntry.note: Same suppression rule as probability_of_joint_goal. Note the SECOND edge here: this is a record, so "suppressed" (absent) and "evaluated, no constraints" (present-and-empty) are two states — the shape of seed instance #3 (PLoT `_meta.constraint_sources` present-empty vs absent).
boundary/EnrichmentOptionComparisonEntry.ref: src/boundary/enrichment.ts — EnrichmentOptionComparisonEntrySchema block comment; seed instance #3

boundary/EnrichmentOptionComparisonEntry.note: The field carries the contract-frozen ABSENCE_FAIL_CLOSED_RULE .describe() text: "Absence of this marker means NOT decision-grade (fail-closed). Consumers MUST NOT treat a missing marker as trustworthy." Absence is therefore a TRUST VERDICT, not a missing convenience — and it is carried by the absence of a boolean whose only other state is `true`, so a consumer that defaults it reads untrusted data as trusted.

Schema block comment: the field is "SUPPRESSED (absent) when any constraint target is unreliable". Absence is a SUPPRESSION SIGNAL carrying a trust verdict, not a missing number; a consumer defaulting it to 0 renders a suppressed metric as a confident zero.

boundary/EnrichmentRobustnessEdgeSchema..note: Field .describe(): "Absence means NOT COMPUTED — never 0 and never 1. A measured 0 is a real measurement and must be preserved." Absence and the numeric 0 are DIFFERENT CLAIMS and the wire carries no discriminator between them beyond key presence — so any consumer coalescing with `?? 0` converts "we did not compute this" into "we measured zero fragility".

boundary/EnrichmentRobustnessSchema.norm.note: LEAD — `z.unknown().optional()` on a field named raw_value inside an error record. Two open questions, not one: (a) absence vs a present-but-undefined value, and (b) whether a raw upstream value belongs on this wire at all (cf. the R2 raw-value leak brief). Answer both before promoting this row out of unresolved.

boundary/OlumiResponseSchema.decision_cl.note: Schema comment: "Absent until the producing turn has actually assessed the decision; consumers MUST NOT default absent dimensions." Absence = unassessed, distinct from any classification.

boundary/OlumiResponseSchema.draft_graph.note: The `.omit({type: true})` twin of DraftGraphBlockSchema.goal_constraints — a SEPARATE ZodObject identity (Zod `.omit()` clones the shape) reached through OlumiResponseSchema.draft_graph, carrying the same field declaration and therefore the same doctrine: absence and `[]` are equivalent. Listed separately because the census keys declaration SITES, and a future edit to one shape does not follow the other.
boundary/OlumiResponseSchema.draft_graph.ref: src/boundary/blocks.ts — DraftGraphBlockSchema.goal_constraints doc comment, reached via src/boundary/olumi-response.ts OlumiResponseSchema.draft_graph

boundary/OlumiResponseSchema.framing_qua.note: Schema comment: "Absent until the producing turn has actually assessed the framing; consumers MUST NOT derive a verdict client-side when it is absent." Absence = not assessed, which is a different claim from every value in {ready, thin, conflict}.

boundary/OlumiResponseSchema.framing_que.note: Schema comment: "when absent, the slot stays empty (fail closed — the UI's heuristic derivation retires rather than remaining as a fallback)." Absence must NOT be filled by a client-side derivation; the whole point of the field is that a derived question was a measured leak.

boundary/OlumiResponseSchema.graph_hash.note: Schema comment: "Optional so pinned consumers are unaffected until they re-vendor 0.22.0; absent = no handshake asserted." Absence disables the GRAPH_DIVERGED check entirely; a defaulted value would silently assert a handshake the producer never made.

orchestrator/RunAnalysisResultSchema.lea.note: SEED INSTANCE #6 (UI), the persisted twin of the block field. Same `z.string().nullable()` shape and the same collapse of every withholding reason into one `null`. Listed separately because it is a SEPARATE declaration site: fixing the block field does not fix this one.

root/RepairEntrySchema.after.note: LEAD — `z.unknown()` with NO `.optional()` anywhere, yet Zod accepts `undefined` for it, so the inferred type is `after?: unknown`. A repair that DELETED a value and a repair whose result was dropped in serialisation are the same bytes. The optionality here is invisible at the declaration site — nothing in `z.unknown()` reads as optional.

root/RepairEntrySchema.before.note: LEAD — `z.unknown().nullable()`. THREE states share one channel: key absent, `null`, and a real value. For a repair log specifically, "there was no prior value" and "the prior value was null" are different repairs. Compounded by JSON: `JSON.stringify` DROPS an `undefined` property, so absence is not even reliably authored by the producer.
